questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis with indurated edges, 2 cm in diameter, with no pain or discharge. Inguinal lymph nodes are firm, non-tender and rubbery. VDRL is reactive at 1:32 dilution. What is the drug of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose. This is the first-line treatment as per WHO and CDC guidelines. The painless, indurated ulcer with non-tender lymphadenopathy is classic for primary syphilis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops erythema, blistering and skin necrosis over 40% BSA after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for UTI 10 days ago. The Nikolsky sign is positive. She also has mucosal involvement of eyes, mouth and genitals. The most appropriate diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) involves detachment of >30% BSA. Stevens-Johnson Syndrome involves <10%, and overlap syndrome 10-30%. TEN is characterized by full-thickness epidermal detachment, positive Nikolsky sign, and mucosal involvement. SSSS occurs mainly in children with subcorneal splitting.

questions.q: A 45-year-old immunocompromised patient presents with white, non-wipeable plaques on the tongue that bleed on scraping. KOH mount shows pseudohyphae with budding yeast forms. The antifungal of choice for systemic spread is:
questions.exp: Oral candidiasis with systemic spread in an immunocompromised host requires Amphotericin B, which has broad antifungal activity and is the gold standard for invasive/systemic candidiasis. Nystatin is used for mucosal/topical disease. Fluconazole can be used for non-severe systemic candidiasis but Amphotericin B is preferred for severe disease.

questions.q: A child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions on the face and nose, starting as vesicles that rupture. The causative organism most commonly responsible is:
questions.exp: Impetigo contagiosa most commonly presents with honey-colored crusted lesions caused by Staphylococcus aureus (or sometimes Group A Streptococcus). Bullous impetigo is almost exclusively caused by S. aureus phage type 71 producing exfoliative toxin.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT (MB regimen) for 6 months develops sudden onset painful erythematous nodules over the face, trunk and limbs with fever and joint pains. ESR is elevated. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL) occurs in BL/LL leprosy, typically after initiating MDT. It presents with tender erythematous nodules, fever, arthritis, and elevated ESR. It is an immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity) reaction. Treatment is thalidomide or prednisolone.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with a butterfly-shaped erythema over the malar region sparing the nasolabial folds, oral ulcers, polyarthritis and photosensitivity for 3 months. ANA is 1:320 (homogeneous pattern). The most specific antibody for her diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Anti-double stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibody is highly specific for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and correlates with disease activity, particularly lupus nephritis. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus. Anti-Ro and Anti-La are associated with Sjogren's syndrome and neonatal lupus.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with flaccid blisters that rupture easily, leaving raw erosions mainly over the trunk, scalp and mucous membranes. Nikolsky sign is positive. Direct immunofluorescence shows IgG deposits in an intercellular 'fishnet' pattern. Diagnosis:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris presents with flaccid blisters and erosions on skin and mucous membranes. DIF shows IgG and C3 in an intercellular (fishnet/chicken wire) pattern against desmoglein 3 (and desmoglein 1). Nikolsky sign is positive. BP has linear IgG at BMZ; DH has granular IgA at BMZ.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with well-defined erythematous plaques with silvery white scales over the elbows, knees and scalp. Auspitz sign is positive. The characteristic pathological finding in this condition is:
questions.exp: Psoriasis is characterized histologically by Munro microabscesses (neutrophil aggregates in parakeratotic stratum corneum) and Kogoj's spongiform pustules (in spinous layer). Civatte bodies are seen in lichen planus. Eosinophilic spongiosis is seen in pemphigus.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male with HIV presents with multiple painless pearly flesh-colored umbilicated papules, 3-5 mm in diameter, scattered over the face, trunk and genitals. The most common causative agent is:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by MCV, a poxvirus. MCV-1 is the most common type causing disease, while MCV-2 is more common in sexually transmitted cases in adults. In HIV patients, lesions can be giant and numerous. The umbilicated papule is the hallmark lesion.

questions.q: A 30-year-old female presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches over the back with loss of sweating and hair. Slit skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows epithelioid granulomas with lymphocytic infiltrate but no bacilli. The leprosy type is:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with 1-2 well-defined, hypopigmented, anaesthetic patches with anhidrosis and hair loss. SSS is negative (paucibacillary). Biopsy shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with lymphocytes, no bacilli. Lepromatous pole has numerous bacilli and diffuse infiltration.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with multiple small (1-3 mm) hypopigmented macules with fine scaling primarily over the upper trunk and back. Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow fluorescence. KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatball' appearance. Treatment of choice:
opts: Oral itraconazole 200 mg daily for 7 days
Oral griseofulvin 500 mg daily for 4 weeks
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor (tinea versicolor) caused by Malassezia furfur shows 'spaghetti and meatball' pattern on KOH. First-line for extensive/recurrent disease is oral itraconazole. For localized disease, topical antifungals (selenium sulfide, azoles) are used. Griseofulvin is ineffective against Malassezia.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a pearly white, translucent papule with rolled telangiectatic borders and central ulceration on his nose, present for 8 months. The most appropriate treatment for this lesion <2 cm:
opts: Wide local excision with 1 cm margin
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) on the face (particularly nose, periorbital region - H-zone) with high risk for recurrence is best treated with Mohs micrographic surgery, which offers the highest cure rate (>99%) with maximum tissue conservation. Wide excision is used for low-risk BCC elsewhere.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman on long-term methotrexate therapy for psoriasis develops nausea, mouth ulcers, elevated LFTs and macrocytic anemia. The supplement that should be co-administered to prevent these side effects is:
opts: Folic acid 5 mg daily (not on methotrexate day)
questions.exp: Methotrexate is a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor. Folic acid 5 mg/day (given on all days except the day of methotrexate) prevents GI side effects, mouth ulcers, and macrocytic anemia without significantly reducing efficacy. Folinic acid (leucovorin) is used for methotrexate toxicity/rescue.

questions.q: A 42-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C presents with purpuric non-blanching lesions over the lower legs, arthralgias and proteinuria. Biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Cryoglobulins are positive. The most likely diagnosis:
questions.exp: Hepatitis C is strongly associated with mixed cryoglobulinemia (Type II). It presents with palpable purpura (leukocytoclastic vasculitis), arthralgia, peripheral neuropathy, and renal involvement. Cryoglobulins precipitate at <37 degrees C. Treatment targets the underlying HCV infection.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with thickening and tightening of the skin starting distally on the fingers and extending proximally past the wrists, Raynaud's phenomenon, dysphagia and pulmonary fibrosis. The most specific antibody for this systemic condition is:
questions.exp: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) is associated with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibody, which correlates with pulmonary fibrosis and poor prognosis. Anti-centromere is associated with limited cutaneous SSc (CREST syndrome). Anti-Jo-1 is in dermatomyositis/polymyositis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless genital ulcer with undermined, ragged edges and irregular borders, which is very tender on palpation. Gram stain shows 'school of fish' pattern. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. It presents with a painful, soft, tender ulcer with ragged/undermined edges ('soft chancre') and painful inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Gram stain shows Gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' pattern. Treatment is azithromycin 1g single dose.

questions.q: A 30-year-old atopic male presents with chronic relapsing eczema, lichenification and severe pruritus over the flexural areas. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. The major diagnostic criterion for his condition according to Hanifin and Rajka is:
questions.exp: Hanifin and Rajka criteria for atopic dermatitis: Major criteria are pruritus, typical morphology and distribution (flexural lichenification in adults), chronic/relapsing course, and personal/family history of atopy. Elevated IgE, ichthyosis, and white dermographism are minor criteria.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the labia majora, vulva and thighs. She has a history of similar recurrent episodes at the same site. The first-line treatment to suppress recurrences is:
questions.exp: For recurrent genital herpes (HSV-2), suppressive therapy with valacyclovir 500 mg once daily (or 1 g OD if >10 episodes/year) reduces recurrence frequency by 70-80% and reduces asymptomatic shedding. Acyclovir 400 mg BD is an alternative. Topical therapy is less effective than oral.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male undergoes liquid nitrogen cryotherapy for a plantar wart. The mechanism by which cryotherapy destroys tissue is:
opts: Ice crystal formation causing cell membrane disruption and vascular stasis
questions.exp: Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen destroys tissue through: intracellular ice crystal formation (at -40 to -50 degrees C), cell membrane disruption, vascular stasis and ischemia, and osmotic damage during thaw. The freeze-thaw cycle is critical; repeated cycles improve efficacy. Melanocytes are particularly sensitive to cold injury.

questions.q: A 58-year-old male presents with violaceous flat-topped polygonal papules over the flexor surfaces of the wrist and oral white lace-like lesions (Wickham's striae). The typical histology shows:
opts: Acanthosis with hypogranulosis and suprabasal acantholysis
Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ with basal cell degeneration and saw-tooth rete ridges
Intraepidermal vesicle formation with eosinophilic infiltrate
Perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with nuclear dust (leukocytoclasis)
questions.exp: Lichen planus histology shows: hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, saw-tooth rete ridges, vacuolar degeneration of basal cells (liquefaction), and a band-like (lichenoid) lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ. Civatte (colloid) bodies represent apoptotic keratinocytes. Max-Joseph spaces may also be seen.

questions.q: A 25-year-old female presents with symmetrical hyperpigmentation over the malar region, forehead and upper lip, worsening during pregnancy. Wood's lamp examination accentuates the pigmentation. The type of melasma indicated by this finding is:
questions.exp: Wood's lamp (365 nm UV) examination helps classify melasma: Epidermal type shows accentuation (melanin predominantly in epidermis), Dermal type shows no accentuation (melanin in dermis), Mixed shows partial accentuation. Epidermal melasma responds better to topical depigmenting agents (hydroquinone, retinoids, azelaic acid).

questions.q: A 12-year-old boy presents with diffuse scaling of the scalp with kerion formation (boggy, tender swelling with pus discharge from follicles). Culture grows Trichophyton tonsurans. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Tinea capitis requires systemic antifungal treatment as topical agents do not penetrate the hair follicle. Oral griseofulvin (20 mg/kg/day for 6-8 weeks with fatty meal) remains the standard. Terbinafine is equally effective for T. tonsurans but griseofulvin is preferred for T. violaceum in India. Kerion may need systemic prednisolone to prevent scarring alopecia.

questions.q: A 70-year-old farmer presents with a rapidly growing verrucous plaque with a hyperkeratotic base on the dorsum of his sun-damaged hand. Biopsy shows well-differentiated squamous cells with keratin pearls infiltrating the dermis. The feature indicating poor prognosis is:
questions.exp: High-risk features for SCC include: diameter >2 cm, depth >2 mm (Clark level IV/V), poor differentiation, perineural invasion, immunosuppression, arising in a scar or chronic ulcer, and location on lip/ear. Well-differentiated histology and diameter <2 cm are low-risk features. Sun damage predisposes but is not a prognostic factor.

questions.q: A 45-year-old patient on long-term isotretinoin therapy for nodulocystic acne develops muscle pain and elevated CPK. What is the most likely side effect and when should the drug be stopped?
opts: Myopathy; stop if CPK >3x upper limit of normal
Rhabdomyolysis; stop if CPK >10x upper limit of normal
Myalgia only; drug need not be stopped, reduce dose
Statin-like effect; co-administer CoQ10 and continue
questions.exp: Isotretinoin can cause myalgia and elevated CPK (especially with vigorous exercise). Rhabdomyolysis is rare but serious. Guidelines recommend stopping isotretinoin if CPK exceeds 3-5x ULN (some guidelines say 10x with symptoms). Combining isotretinoin with tetracyclines is contraindicated (raised ICP/pseudotumor cerebri).

questions.q: A newborn presents with a large bullous lesion rupturing at birth to leave a raw erosion, positive family history, and electron microscopy showing cleavage within the lamina lucida. The integrin likely mutated is:
questions.exp: In Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa (JEB), cleavage occurs within the lamina lucida. The most severe form (Herlitz JEB) is caused by mutations in LAMA3, LAMB3, or LAMC2 (laminin-332 genes). Alpha-6-beta-4 integrin mutations cause JEB with pyloric atresia. Collagen XVII mutations cause non-Herlitz JEB. Collagen VII mutations cause Dystrophic EB (sublamina densa).

questions.q: A 55-year-old diabetic woman presents with thickened, yellow-brown, crumbly nails with subungual debris, affecting all toenails. KOH of subungual scrapings shows septate hyphae. The most effective oral treatment regimen is:
opts: Itraconazole pulse therapy 200 mg BD for 1 week/month x 2 pulses
questions.exp: For onychomycosis of the toenails, terbinafine 250 mg daily for 12 weeks has the highest mycological cure rate (~70-80%) among oral antifungals. Itraconazole pulse (400 mg/day x 1 week/month for 3 months for toenails) is an alternative. Griseofulvin has high relapse rates. Terbinafine is fungicidal against dermatophytes.

questions.q: A 38-year-old male presents with diffuse non-scarring alopecia in a band-like pattern (ophiasis pattern). Dermoscopy shows 'exclamation mark hairs' and yellow dots. The diagnosis and expected course is:
opts: Alopecia areata; spontaneous regrowth in 50% within 1 year
Telogen effluvium; resolves after removing trigger
questions.exp: Alopecia areata presents with non-scarring patches. Ophiasis pattern (band-like along margins) has a worse prognosis. Dermoscopy shows exclamation mark hairs (pathognomonic), black dots, yellow dots, and vellus hairs. ~50% regrow within 1 year but recurrence is common. Ophiasis and alopecia totalis/universalis have poorer prognosis.

questions.q: A 72-year-old man presents with tense bullae on an erythematous and urticarial base over the trunk and limbs, sparing mucous membranes. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition at the basement membrane zone. The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) presents with tense bullae (unlike flaccid bullae in pemphigus), sparing mucous membranes in most cases. DIF shows linear IgG/C3 at BMZ. Target antigens are BP180 (BPAG2/collagen XVII) and BP230 (BPAG1). Anti-BP180 correlates with disease activity. Treatment is superpotent topical steroids or systemic prednisolone.

questions.q: A 30-year-old pregnant woman (16 weeks) presents with scabies. The safest topical treatment option for her is:
questions.exp: Permethrin 5% cream is considered the safest and most effective treatment for scabies in pregnancy. It is a synthetic pyrethroid with minimal systemic absorption. Lindane is contraindicated in pregnancy due to neurotoxicity. Benzyl benzoate is used but may irritate. Oral ivermectin is not recommended in pregnancy (safety not established).

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with a 2 cm pigmented lesion on the back showing asymmetry, irregular borders, variegated color (brown, black, pink), and diameter >6 mm. Dermoscopy shows atypical pigment network, regression structures and blue-white veil. Biopsy confirms malignant melanoma, Clark level IV, Breslow thickness 2.2 mm. Recommended surgical excision margin is:
questions.exp: Surgical excision margins for melanoma per Breslow thickness: in situ = 0.5-1 cm; <1 mm = 1 cm; 1-2 mm = 1-2 cm; 2-4 mm = 2 cm; >4 mm = 2-3 cm. For this lesion with Breslow 2.2 mm, the recommended margin is 2 cm. Sentinel lymph node biopsy should also be performed for melanomas >1 mm or with ulceration.
